en: Because of my line of work, my first words
come out like that, I'm afraid.
It can't be helped.
I appreciate you saying so.
We take care of everything,
from carrying out the departed to burial,
right through to the upkeep of the grave.
Please call on us should the need arise.
(None of this concerns me.)
Ah, you're the one I met earlier...
Since I run the undertaker's,
my first words tend to come out
like that.
By day, I tend the cemetery like this.
If you need me, I'd be grateful if you
would come by the cemetery.
Mind you, I'm often away from it, such as
when I'm seeing a coffin off.
My condolences...
For words like that to become a habit,
you must be very busy indeed.
Yes, thank heaven, business is booming...
Er, I mean, I've been kept very busy.
You see,
Almost every day, dead children are
brought here from the factory that lies
to the west of Calstatt.
note: row order of the sentence rearranged across #4344-#4346

en: In that factory's wretched conditions,
they work children literally to "death."
Does no one make an issue of it?
In Berlin or London, it might well become
an issue, but here in Calstatt, well...
I doubt it ever will.
It's common enough in any provincial town.
You needn't apologize anymore
The one buried a while ago
didn't seem to be a child...
Yes. It was the sickness going around.
It's an illness they call "cholera."
Have you heard of it?
No. Never heard of it.
There's been a great deal of it lately.
It's dangerous, with violent stomach pains.
Apparently it comes from something eaten.
Not just the old folk, but even the young
are losing their lives to it.
You take care as well, sir.
Since this trade deals in others' misfortune,
there's a side to it people struggle with, but
if I must see people off either way, I'd far
rather quietly help a family send off
someone who lived a long life.
It does pay, I'll grant you, but seeing off
the children who died at the factory,
and those lost to cholera, one after another,
is truly painful for me.
Another child came from the factory today.
Calstatt has changed a great deal since
the old days, but the things that ought to
change never seem to, do they?
Instead of funerals, I'll have you purify.
As a Dhampir, you won't hover between
life and death. So relax, and let me feed.
(A visitor, this late at night?)
Sir, have mercy, at this time of night?
No, this time I've come on business.
In that case,
note: no used_in (unverified); assumed to lead into #4387

en: we'll gladly lend you our assistance.
Business, yes, but not a funeral. Purification.
Purification?
That's right.
note: also the player's reply to Rosner (msg 173340)

en: Your job is to defeat the Nosferatu and
see them off back to being human!
N-Nosferatu? Don't tell me... you're

en: a vampire!

en: H-
Heeelp me!
You won't get away.
Working every day would suit
your way of life better.
